answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-space-time admission: each identity must pledge a large block of real disk, say a hundred gigabytes, and keep answering unpredictable audits proving that data still sits uniquely on its own hardware. One honest node is a single island of committed capacity, but a thousand sybils need a thousandfold of genuine storage that cannot be deduplicated, so the operator cost spirals upward with every clone. When a gale of simultaneous audits sweeps the network, any identity sharing another disk fails its proof at once and is slashed.
